documented_range.note: NO EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES THAT THIS PARTICULAR BUILDING EXISTED. It is the roof a reconstructed household requires - eIGHT DOCUMENTED DOCTORS AND NOT ONE OFFICE. A physician's office and apothecary's back room on the Lake Street frontage, where a doctor is found by people who need one. It is left unnamed on purpose: four of the eight are documented households in this dataset and attaching any of them to an invented building would turn a hypothesis into a false attribution. The argument for the trade's presence in the town is in the household record and in the occupation census at data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json; the argument for THIS BUILDING is only that the household needs somewhere to be.

change_note: Raised by the inferred-household programme. A better-evidenced named building substitutes for this roof rather than standing beside it.

placement.position_note: INTERPRETIVE PLACEMENT, NOT A RECOVERED LOT. EIGHT DOCUMENTED DOCTORS AND NOT ONE OFFICE. A physician's office and apothecary's back room on the Lake Street frontage, where a doctor is found by people who need one. It is left unnamed on purpose: four of the eight are documented households in this dataset and attaching any of them to an invented building would turn a hypothesis into a false attribution. The band follows ROADMAP K1's placement rule - businesses toward the river and the built streets, residences further out - using the same frontage bands the reconstruction recipes already work in, which come from the 80 ft platted street module in data/traces/street_control.json. The centre was tested against every structure footprint in the dataset, against the reserved slots of the two uninstantiated phase-2 recipes, against the platted street corridors of the K7 block grid so that no invented building stands in the roadway, and against the committed heightfield for coverage, dry ground and step tolerance; it is free ground and nothing more. The dataset's 20 m working georeference uncertainty applies on top of an already invented position.

THE OTHER FORM ON OFFER IS REFUSED, AND HERE IS THE NUMBER. The C1 roof line offers "front gable or shed, 5:12-9:12", and this town builds only the gable. A shed is one plane over the whole 7.8 m of this plan where a gable climbs half of it, so across the 441 plans C1's own footprint band allows, 231 of them cannot reach the 15-20 ft ridge band the same family authors — at any eave in its 9-11 ft band and at any pitch between 22.6 and 36.9 degrees. This building's own plan is not one of them; the C1 family is refused as a whole rather than plan by plan.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: Dr. Josiah C. Goodhue
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED MAN ON A RECONSTRUCTED ROOF. The papers name him and this household's dwelling does not: what is attested is the person and his trade, and what remains the reconstruction's is everything about where he lived. He is printed as 'Dr. Josian C. Goovnur' and the corpus reads his trade as physician. Cited at the Democrat of 4 February 1834, column 1. THIS ROOF DID NOT COME FROM HIS RECORD. The household was raised by the occupation census because the town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings needed a physician and no documented one was available; the register (data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json, action `replace_invented`) is what says one now is. The dwelling's existence, position and footprint are unchanged and still conjectural, and nothing here claims he slept in it — only that the town's need for this trade is met by a man the papers name rather than by one this project invented. The invented name this record used to carry, and its name_basis block, are retired: an invented name is not kept beside a documented one. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1); the placement is L205. He is placed nowhere in particular by his own record, which is the condition of taking ANY roof of his trade — a man the papers put on a named street takes only a roof the plat stands on that street (T-0367), and one they place somewhere this scene cannot honour is refused outright. READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

residents.research_note:
RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 physician households in this layer, in the south division. EIGHT PHYSICIANS ARE DOCUMENTED IN THE 1833 TOWN AND THIS DATASET HELD NOT ONE DOCTOR'S OFFICE. Four are written as households in the documented layer. One further physician household is inferred to occupy the office this parcel builds, because naming that office for a documented doctor would attach a real man to an invented building. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

RETIRED AN INVENTED NAME (T-0264). This household was raised by the occupation census and named from the invented-name pools. The newspaper register matched it to Dr. Josiah C. Goodhue, a documented physician the corpus names 1 time(s) and places nowhere in particular, and he now holds the roof. What changed is WHO: the argument for the household, its dwelling and its position are untouched and still the reconstruction's, and the person's grade is `inferred` — a real man with reconstructed details — rather than `attested`, which would claim the dwelling too. tools/replace_invented_residents.py derives this deal and prints every candidate it refused.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, RAISED FOR A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). EIGHT DOCUMENTED DOCTORS AND NOT ONE OFFICE. A physician's office and apothecary's back room on the Lake Street frontage, where a doctor is found by people who need one. It is left unnamed on purpose: four of the eight are documented households in this dataset and attaching any of them to an invented building would turn a hypothesis into a false attribution. It is NOT one of the anonymous count-units of the 665-roof programme: those are placed by aggregate mix and carry no occupant, while this one exists because the occupation census says the town held a household of this trade and no anonymous roof of the right family stood free in this district. It consumes one slot of its district's programme target rather than adding to it - see the accounting block in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json.
